title: Cyclone Murasu's eye crosses Andhra coast near Ongole; Vijayawada roads waterlogged
dek: The IMD says most of the storm's wall cloud is over land and the landfall near Ongole should be complete by about 8 am, with winds gusting to 120 kmph and heavy rain across south coastal Andhra Pradesh.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The eye of Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu was crossing the south Andhra Pradesh coast close to Ongole early on Tuesday, 3 November, with heavy rain and very strong winds reported at Kothapatnam beach, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in an update reported by ANI at 5.46 am. A major part of the storm's wall cloud had moved over land and the landfall process would continue for about another two hours, the IMD said, which would put its completion at around 8 am.

The landfall process began at 1 am. Gale winds of 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph, were expected along and off the coast until the morning, and a storm surge of 1 to 1.5 metres above the astronomical tide was likely to flood low-lying parts of Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam districts, the IMD said. No deaths had been reported by 6.20 am, and officials had not yet given figures for damage or power cuts.

## Tuesday morning

In Vijayawada, about 200 km north of the landfall point, heavy rain that began late on Monday night continued into Tuesday, waterlogging Bandar Road, Polyclinic Road and parts of One Town, ANI reported at 6.17 am. The outer rain bands also brought continuous rain to Puducherry from midnight, The News Mill reported. The IMD said heavy spells of rain were likely along the south Andhra coast over the next 12 hours, and it was tracking the storm with Doppler radars at Chennai and Machilipatnam.

At a teleconference in the early hours, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu told officials to stay on high alert and make sure there was no loss of life, saying deaths like those during Cyclone Arnab last week should not be repeated, according to ANI and The News Mill. He said winds were expected to be weaker than during Arnab, asked the power department to restore electricity immediately wherever it failed, and ordered steps to prevent breaches in canals and irrigation tanks. Officials told him heavy rain was forecast in 125 mandals.

Prakasam's Superintendent of Police, Harshavardhan Raju, said three NDRF teams and one SDRF team were stationed in the district. "From the police point of view, we are very much prepared in terms of rescue operations," he said, according to The News Mill; police had set up communication links in the most exposed villages, prepared holding areas on the highways and placed earth-movers to clear roads. The Prakasam district collector, P. Raja Babu, made a midnight visit to the collectorate's control room and ordered officials to clear fallen trees, restore traffic and repair power lines, and to restore electricity in Kothapatnam as soon as possible.

## Before landfall

At 1.30 am the storm's centre was about 40 km southeast of Ongole, 60 km northeast of Kavali and 70 km south of Bapatla, the IMD said in a release reported by PTI. In Prakasam district, seven coastal mandals and 26 vulnerable villages had been identified, vulnerable people had been moved to cyclone shelters and pregnant women close to delivery had been shifted to hospitals, the collector said, according to Deccan Chronicle. On Monday the state disaster management authority's managing director, Prakhar Jain, said about 2,000 people had been evacuated, with about 30,000 more to be moved, according to The Pioneer. Earlier IMD bulletins had put the storm surge at 1.5 to 2 metres. Murasu, a Tamil word for a drum, is the second cyclone to threaten the Andhra coast in a week, after Cyclone Arnab.

## Warnings in force

A red cyclone warning, the last of the IMD's four stages, is in force for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining north Tamil Nadu coasts, according to OMMCOM. Red alerts for extremely heavy rain cover Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam and Nellore districts, Sakshi Post reported, citing the IMD. East and West Godavari, Eluru, NTR, Palnadu, Tirupati and Chittoor are on orange alert.

After landfall the storm is forecast to weaken quickly as it moves north over Andhra Pradesh towards Telangana: to a cyclonic storm with winds of 90-100 kmph by 5.30 am on Tuesday, 60-70 kmph by Tuesday evening, and a deep depression by Wednesday morning, according to the IMD Kolkata bulletin issued at 9 pm on Monday.

## Andhra Pradesh prepares

Reviewing preparations on Monday, Naidu was told that 31,000 electricity poles had been sent to the field, that about 8,000 poles in the south coastal and Rayalaseema districts could be affected, and that 1,000 power-restoration workers were arriving from Chennai, IANS reported. About 6,800 irrigation tanks in six districts are at risk of breaching, officials said.

At least 19 domestic flights were cancelled on Monday at Vijayawada, Tirupati and Visakhapatnam airports, PTI reported; Vijayawada airport director M. Lakshmi Kantha Reddy said IndiGo had cancelled 10 flights and Air India Express two. Chennai airport said 11 flights had been cancelled as a precaution. By Monday night the National Disaster Response Force had deployed 37 teams across five states, 13 of them in Andhra Pradesh, its DIG, Mohsen Shahedi, said, according to ANI.

The disaster management authority's helplines are 112, 1070 and 1800 425 0101, and the state's Mana Mitra WhatsApp helpline is 9552300009.

## What it means for Bengal

IMD Kolkata's latest bulletin, issued at 9 pm on Monday, says there is "No weather warning for West Bengal in association with this system", which it is monitoring continuously. Distant Warning Signal No. 2 has now been hoisted at the Kolkata and Haldia ports, up from the Distant Cautionary Signal No. 1 hoisted on Saturday, with sectional signals II and IV at Sagar Island.

Light to moderate rain is likely at one or two places on Tuesday in Kolkata and several south Bengal districts, with dry weather across the state from Wednesday to 9 November, the bulletin said. There is no fishing warning for the Bengal coast.

## Odisha braces again

Southern Odisha is still recovering from Cyclone Arnab. IMD Bhubaneswar has issued an orange warning for heavy to very heavy rain in Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Gajapati and Ganjam on 3 and 4 November, Argus reported. By Monday night more than 1.6 lakh people had been moved to safety across southern Odisha, against a plan to evacuate 3.33 lakh, the state government said, according to Deccan Chronicle.

## What happens next

The IMD expects the strongest winds along the coast until Tuesday morning, after which the storm should weaken quickly over land. Many districts will feel the heaviest rain on Tuesday, after the storm has crossed the coast, and Telangana is under a warning for isolated extremely heavy rain on Tuesday. The first assessments of damage, power cuts and crop losses are likely after daybreak.

## Key numbers

- Landfall: process began at 1 am IST on 3 November close to Ongole, Prakasam district; eye crossing the coast at 5.46 am, completion expected about two hours later (IMD)
- Peak forecast wind: 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph
- Storm surge: 1-1.5 m above astronomical tide in the IMD's landfall release (1.5-2 m in earlier bulletins), highest over Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam
- Evacuated: Andhra Pradesh about 2,000 by Monday, with 30,000 more planned (state officials); Odisha more than 1.6 lakh (state government, via Deccan Chronicle)
- Red alert districts: Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam, Nellore
- Bengal: no warning; Distant Warning Signal No. 2 at Kolkata and Haldia ports
